title: LoL Esports |
content:
Welcome to the LCS Promotion Tournament! Tier-2 teams have been battling throughout the year where only one challenge remains. The stakes couldn’t be higher as the LCS Promotion Tournament will determine which team earns the coveted LCS Guest Slot for the 2027 season. Only the top two NACL and LRN teams will advance to face the defending Guest Team, Disguised. Disguised successfully fought off all opposing challengers in 2026. The question is, can they do it again?

Across seven days, all five teams will compete in a double-elimination bracket featuring Full Fearless, First Selection, Best-of-Fives. The defending Guest Team will enter with a bracket advantage but must still win their spot—no automatic requalification. All matches begin at 1pm PDT.

This year, we’re thrilled to partner with LYON to produce the LCS Promotion Tournament fresh off of the LCS Homegrounds. The first six days of the tournament will be played remotely similar to last year, but we’re excited to introduce a live audience LAN Finals hosted by LYON at the Arena Esports Stadium at CINEMEX Artz Pedregal in Mexico City, Mexico. In order to ensure a competitive tournament during the remote stage, LRN teams, where necessary, will be provided flights, hotels, and practice rooms in Mexico City for the duration of the tournament.

The tournament winner secures the LCS Guest Slot, granting the right to compete in the LCS and qualify for major global events, including First Stand, MSI, and Worlds. The Guest Slot also comes with financial support: an operating stipend, access to the Global Revenue Pool from LoL Esports in-game content sales, and the same business model benefits as Tier-1 teams.

To catch all of the action live, stay tuned starting October 5 onTwitch.tv/LCSandYouTube.com/@LCS.

In case you missed it, we also recently announced a brand new international Tier-2 Tournament called theWorld Star Challengers Invitational. The article has the full tournament details, but we’re excited to provide the NACL Summer Split Champion a qualification spot as the Tier-2 representative from North America.

title: League of Legends Patch 26.18 Notes
summary: League of Legends Patch 26.18 Notes  League of Legends
content:
Immortalized Legend Tristana, Risen Legend Orianna, and Risen Legend Tristana will be available September 10, 2026.

Bard has been a meta staple for much of the year. Earlier we toned his damage down to what we think are reasonable levels, so this time we are going to target his durability which has also stood out as high given his mobility and long range ultimate utility.

Cassio has always scaled with skill, but this year has propelled her to new heights of pro play dominance despite being weaker for average players. These adjustments should tap down her laning power, especially in pro where defensive purchases are valued more than raw AP, while giving her back some scaling power. It will still be critical to use empowered E's, but raising her floor lets us be a bit more flexible with tuning.

As one of our assassins that offer opponents a wider mix of gameplay options, Ekko has found a slightly weak steady state since Dusk & Dawn's update mid year. We believe he has some room for power, especially in mid where he scales slightly worse, without buffing his Hail of Blades pattern.

Kassadin had a strong start to 2026 but hasn't regained his…footing…since our earlier nerfs. His Q should feel more punchy with his scaling, and we're aiming to provide more early agency through good Riftwalk usage without touching his late game fantasy.

Yi drew the short end of the stick on the Rageblade bugfix from earlier this year due to his double strike interactions. While the actual impact for most Rageblade users was minor (and we are compensating Rageblade as well for that this patch), he was impacted harder than the other users. He's also just been unable to scale as well as a melee carry compared to his normal power level, so we are also giving him a buff up.

title: Gen.G Aims for Back-to-Back Single-Season LCK Titles
summary: Gen.G Aims for Back-to-Back Single-Season LCK Titles  invenglobal.com
content:
Riot Games announced that it will host the '2026 Woori Bank LCK FINALS' at the KSPO Dome in Olympic Park, Songpa-gu, Seoul, from the 12th to the 13th. Gen.G has advanced directly to the grand final, while Hanwha Life Esports and T1 will face off in the Finals Qualifier.

The LCK, the Korean professional league for League of Legends esports, has been operating under a single-season format since 2025. Gen.G, who won the inaugural single-season championship last year, finished this year's regular season with a 19-7 record. Tied with Hanwha Life Esports in both win-loss record and game differential, Gen.G took first place thanks to a superior head-to-head record.

In the playoffs, Gen.G defeated KT Rolster 3-0 and Hanwha Life Esports 3-1 to secure their spot in the grand final first. Against Hanwha Life Esports in 2026, Gen.G holds a 5-1 record, while their regular season head-to-head against T1 ended in a 2-2 tie. If Gen.G wins the grand final on the 13th, they will achieve two consecutive single-season LCK titles.

The Finals Qualifier will take place on the 12th as a best-of-five match between Hanwha Life Esports and T1. The two teams have met seven times in the LCK this year, with Hanwha Life Esports taking 5 wins. If Hanwha Life Esports wins, they will face Gen.G in the finals once again following Summer 2024 and 2025. If T1 wins, they will reach the LCK finals for the first time since Spring 2024.

The grand final on the 13th will be dual-broadcast live on LCK channels and MBC. On the LCK channel, caster Jun Yong-jun and commentators Lee 'CloudTemplar' Hyun-woo and Lim 'Pony' Ju-wan will provide commentary. On MBC, caster Sung Seung-heon will team up with commentators Jeong 'NoFe' No-chul and Go 'Kkogkogat' Soo-jin.

At Haneul Square outside the KSPO Dome, side events will run on both days of the event from 9:00 AM to 7:00 PM. Visitors without match tickets can also participate, with booths and photo walls for the three final teams, as well as photo zones for all 10 LCK teams.
